title: Mlai senior systemdesign data pipeline scaling
topic: Mlai senior systemdesign data pipeline scaling
question: How would you redesign this data pipeline to handle that scale reliably?
idealAnswer:
Move from single-machine, in-memory processing to a distributed data processing framework, e.g. Spark or similar, that can process data in parallel across many machines without needing it all to fit in memory at once

Store data in an efficient columnar format, e.g. Parquet, partitioned sensibly, e.g. by date, so downstream jobs can read only the data they need rather than scanning everything

Break the pipeline into smaller, independently retriable stages with checkpointing, so a failure partway through only requires re-running the failed stage, not the entire 30-hour job from scratch

Consider incremental or streaming processing where feasible, processing only new data since the last run rather than reprocessing the full historical dataset every time

Add monitoring and alerting on pipeline health, job duration, data volume processed, failure rate, so degradation is caught proactively rather than discovered when someone notices training didn't finish

A strong answer weighs the cost and complexity tradeoff of infrastructure choices against actual scale needs, rather than reaching for the most complex distributed system by default
